title: Why I don't recommend Tailwind CSS | Andros Fenollosa

content_html:
Tailwind CSS is a very popular CSS framework among web developers. With no prior graphic design knowledge, it solves the standardization of spacing, colors, and sizes for you. And on top of that, if you are even slightly disorganized, it forces you into a working methodology based on building large structures out of simple utilities (Utility-First Fundamentals). Add to all that a documentation that is easy to understand with a flawless search.

In the past I used it on several projects, it helped me build user interfaces quickly. And despite all of that, it is a tool I would not recommend in every context. I am going to give you my point of view, my reasons, why you should think twice before using Tailwind CSS on medium or large projects. The only thing I ask of you is an open mind, self-criticism, and a willingness to learn.

You have to learn dozens of classes

Tailwind has thousands of utility classes. Even though the documentation is very good and the editor autocomplete helps a lot, there is a ceiling of basic classes you have to internalize. Most likely, at first you will develop with a browser tab open and the search box working nonstop. You spend time understanding the most appropriate way to apply each class. A slow process at the start. And if you have created your own classes that mix with Tailwind's, the difficulty grows.

It breaks the separation between structure and design

Tailwind CSS is a gigantic utility library, atomic classes with specific jobs. Unless you group classes with @apply, you end up including dozens of them in your HTML. This breaks the classic rule of separating structure from design, or HTML from CSS. It bloats the HTML, readability suffers, and you lose reusability.

That said, this one is worth pausing on, because it is the criticism that gets rebutted the most. Adam Wathan, the creator of Tailwind, wrote the foundational text of the defense, and his argument is a good one. The separation of concerns does not disappear, it changes direction. With "semantic" CSS, your CSS depends on the HTML; you can restyle the HTML, but your CSS is not reusable. With utilities, your HTML depends on the CSS; the CSS is reusable, but your HTML does not restyle itself. The coupling exists in both cases, only the direction of the arrow changes.

The argument holds in a world of components, where React or Vue already put logic, markup, and style in the same file. There, the separation by file type was already broken by you beforehand. But in a server-rendered project, with templates and classic CSS, the separation still makes complete sense. It is not a universal law, it is a decision that depends on your architecture.

Its names are not consistent

Its naming is not always coherent, at times it is opaque and tends to confuse. Look at the alignment classes. What is the difference between items-center, justify-center, text-center, and place-content-center? The name is not intuitive and does not follow a clear pattern. In case you are curious, items-center aligns items in a flex container, justify-center aligns them on the main axis, text-center centers text, and place-content-center centers content in a grid. Let me rename them looking for coherence: flex-align-items-center, flex-justify-content-center, text-align-center, and grid-place-items-center. Do you notice the difference?

There are more examples: justify-center but items-center (not align-center); border gives 1px but border-2 gives 2px. Small frictions that add up.

The design system is not enforced as much as it seems

One of the big arguments in favor of Tailwind is that its spacing and color scale forces you to be consistent. And that is true, but with a catch, the arbitrary values. You can write w-[347px], text-[#1a2b3c], or p-[5.5rem] without anything warning you. They are an escape hatch that breaks the system. Nothing stops you from using sky-400 and blue-400 in the same project. Consistency still depends on your discipline, not on the framework. The system helps you, but it does not save you from yourself.

It is not a good gateway to learning CSS

Tailwind is easy to use if you already master styling. But for those with little CSS experience, it creates a false sense of learning. It conveys that it is a minimalist way of writing CSS, taking away the effort of keeping your code tidy. Using so many pre-built classes hinders a developer's ability to truly master CSS. The time you save naming classes you lose learning to use the framework in the most efficient way.

On the other hand, if you go deep into Tailwind, you drift away from learning the fundamentals of the platform. pt-4 forces you to mentally translate to padding-top: 1rem. You gain fluency in the abstraction, not in CSS. To my students and coworkers I recommend learning CSS before Tailwind. And if you are already an experienced developer, you might not even need the framework.

It is hard to read

Let me show you a button with an indigo background, white text, semibold font, rounded corners, hover, and focus.

First in vanilla CSS. I will take the liberty of using variables for colors and spacing, and nesting for hover and focus, something compatible today with every browser.

:root {
  --color-white: #fff;
  --color-black: #000;
  --color-indigo: #4f46e5;
  --color-indigo-hover: #4338ca;
  --gap-s: 0.5rem;
  --gap-m: 1rem;
}

.button {
    padding: var(--gap-s) var(--gap-m);
    background-color: var(--color-indigo);
    color: var(--color-white);
    font-weight: 700;
    border-radius: var(--gap-s);
    &:hover, &:focus {
        background-color: var(--color-indigo-hover);
    }
}

Now in Tailwind CSS using @apply.

.button {
    @apply py-2 px-4 bg-indigo-500 text-white font-semibold rounded-lg hover:bg-indigo-700 focus:bg-indigo-700;
}

Vanilla CSS is self-explanatory, whereas with Tailwind you have to check the documentation. What color is bg-indigo-500? How round is rounded-lg? Is bg-indigo-700 darker than bg-indigo-500? The first snippet is easier to maintain, the learning curve for a new developer is low, and the CSS tends to be modular. You do put in more effort with vanilla CSS, yes, but only at the start. Afterward you have full control of variables, cascade, and naming.

A curious detail. The example above uses @apply, and Adam Wathan himself has admitted that @apply "basically only exists to trick people" and that if he started Tailwind from scratch he would not include it. In other words, the route you use to recover the readability of a normal class contradicts Tailwind's philosophy. And if you do not use @apply, then you swallow the class soup in your HTML.

The HTML lies to you about priority

You may have heard that Tailwind "ignores the cascade". That is an imprecise way to put it, because the real problem is more subtle and interesting.

Being able to control which selector wins based on its position in the stylesheet is fundamental to any architecture. A typical mistake among inexperienced web designers is to believe that the order of the classes in the HTML determines which one wins. It does not. Look at this code.

<p class="color-red color-green">I am some text</p>

What color is it? You do not know. You need to see the CSS cascade.

.color-green {
    color: green;
}

.color-red {
    color: red;
}

Now yes, it is red, because .color-red is defined later. So far, normal CSS.

The problem with Tailwind is that you cannot resolve this ambiguity even by reordering your classes. Watch.

<p class="text-red-500 text-green-500">I am some text</p>

You might think green wins, since it comes last in the attribute. Well, no, you get red. What wins is decided by the order in which Tailwind generates those classes in the final stylesheet, not the order in which you write them in the HTML. The markup lies to you. Reading the HTML you cannot know the result. And you do not fix it by changing the order of the classes, because that order is controlled by the compiler. You are left with !important or with avoiding conflicting utilities. This is what is called a leaky abstraction. It promises you simplicity and forces you to know how it works underneath. Another classic case, class="mt-4 mt-0" does not do what its order suggests.

Working with Dev Tools is not comfortable

When you build components with tons of classes, checking in the inspector which styles apply becomes slow. You have to scroll looking for what wins and what gets overridden. With vanilla CSS you quickly see which styles are there and in what order, and an error is easier to locate. It is true that editor extensions ease this at writing time, but in the browser, debugging in production, the class soup is still there.

Conclusion

What if you just use modern CSS?

Here is, for me, the truly fresh debate. It is no longer "utilities versus CSS by hand". It is "native modern CSS versus a utility layer on top".

Look at what the platform gives you today, without installing anything:

  • Cascade layers (@layer) to order priority without fighting specificity.
  • Native nesting, now without a preprocessor.
  • Custom properties (CSS variables) for your tokens.
  • :has(), the parent selector we had been asking for over twenty years.
  • Container queries for per-component responsiveness.
  • color-mix() to derive colors.

And you know what the ironic part is? That Tailwind is built right on top of those same features. It uses native cascade layers, @property, container queries, and OKLCH colors. Which gives ammunition to the most uncomfortable argument. If the platform already brings all that, how much of Tailwind is still essential?

The counterpart is clear. Native CSS gives you the features, but it does not give you the system of constraints, nor the style kept next to the markup (colocation), nor autocomplete. On small or server-rendered projects, modern CSS on its own is a great option. On a large product built with components and with many people touching it, Tailwind still has arguments. There is no universal winner, there is a context.

But let us put things in perspective. It is not a bad tool. It is a tool with a cost you pay in the future, and one that nowadays also competes with a native CSS far more capable than a few years ago. Before choosing it, learn CSS. Then decide with knowledge. The initial effort you save today, you may pay back with interest tomorrow. Or maybe not. Now, at least, you have both sides to decide for yourself.

Sources

  • CSS Utility Classes and "Separation of Concerns", Adam Wathan (the foundational text of the defense: the direction of the dependency).
  • Open-sourcing our progress on Tailwind CSS v4.0, official Tailwind blog (new engine, CSS-first config with @theme, and the performance figures).
  • Why I Don't Like Tailwind CSS, Aleksandr Hovhannisyan.
  • Disadvantages of Tailwind CSS, Script Raccoon.

blocks.html_en: Its naming is not always coherent, at times it is opaque and tends to confuse. Look at the alignment classes. What is the difference between items-center, justify-center, text-center, and place-content-center? The name is not intuitive and does not follow a clear pattern. In case you are curious, items-center aligns items in a flex container, justify-center aligns them on the main axis, text-center centers text, and place-content-center centers content in a grid. Let me rename them looking for coherence: flex-align-items-center, flex-justify-content-center, text-align-center, and grid-place-items-center. Do you notice the difference?

sentences.en: Its naming is not always coherent, at times it is opaque and tends to confuse.
sentences.zh: 它的命名并不总是连贯的，有时是不透明的并且容易造成混乱。

sentences.en: Look at the alignment classes.
sentences.zh: 查看对齐类。

sentences.en: What is the difference between items-center, justify-center, text-center, and place-content-center?
sentences.zh: items-center、justify-center、text-center 和 place-content-center 之间有什么区别？

sentences.en: The name is not intuitive and does not follow a clear pattern.
sentences.zh: 该名称不直观且不遵循清晰的模式。

sentences.en: In case you are curious, items-center aligns items in a flex container, justify-center aligns them on the main axis, text-center centers text, and place-content-center centers content in a grid.
sentences.zh: 如果您好奇，items-center 可以在 Flex 容器中对齐项目，justify-center 可以在主轴上对齐它们，text-center 可以使文本居中，而 place-content-center 可以使网格中的内容居中。

sentences.en: Let me rename them looking for coherence: flex-align-items-center, flex-justify-content-center, text-align-center, and grid-place-items-center.
sentences.zh: 让我重命名它们以寻求连贯性：flex-align-items-center、flex-justify-content-center、text-align-center 和 grid-place-items-center。

sentences.en: Do you notice the difference?
sentences.zh: 你注意到其中的区别了吗？

blocks.html_en: There are more examples: justify-center but items-center (not align-center); border gives 1px but border-2 gives 2px. Small frictions that add up.

sentences.en: There are more examples: justify-center but items-center (not align-center); border gives 1px but border-2 gives 2px.
sentences.zh: 还有更多的例子： justify-center 但 items-center （不是align-center）； border 给出 1px，但 border-2 给出 2px。

sentences.en: Small frictions that add up.
sentences.zh: 小摩擦累积起来。

blocks.html_en: The design system is not enforced as much as it seems

sentences.en: The design system is not enforced as much as it seems
sentences.zh: 设计系统并没有像看起来那样得到执行

blocks.html_en: One of the big arguments in favor of Tailwind is that its spacing and color scale forces you to be consistent. And that is true, but with a catch, the arbitrary values. You can write w-[347px], text-[#1a2b3c], or p-[5.5rem] without anything warning you. They are an escape hatch that breaks the system. Nothing stops you from using sky-400 and blue-400 in the same project. Consistency still depends on your discipline, not on the framework. The system helps you, but it does not save you from yourself.

sentences.en: One of the big arguments in favor of Tailwind is that its spacing and color scale forces you to be consistent.
sentences.zh: 支持 Tailwind 的一大论据是它的间距和色阶迫使你保持一致。

sentences.en: And that is true, but with a catch, the arbitrary values.
sentences.zh: 这是事实，但有一个问题，即任意值。

sentences.en: You can write w-[347px], text-[#1a2b3c], or p-[5.5rem] without anything warning you.
sentences.zh: 您可以编写 w-[347px]、text-[#1a2b3c] 或 p-[5.5rem]，而无需任何警告。

sentences.en: They are an escape hatch that breaks the system.
sentences.zh: 它们是破坏系统的逃生口。

sentences.en: Nothing stops you from using sky-400 and blue-400 in the same project.
sentences.zh: 没有什么可以阻止您在同一项目中使用 sky-400 和 blue-400。

sentences.en: Consistency still depends on your discipline, not on the framework.
sentences.zh: 一致性仍然取决于你的纪律，而不是框架。

sentences.en: The system helps you, but it does not save you from yourself.
sentences.zh: 系统可以帮助你，但它不能拯救你自己。

blocks.html_en: It is not a good gateway to learning CSS

sentences.en: It is not a good gateway to learning CSS
sentences.zh: 这不是学习 CSS 的好门户

blocks.html_en: Tailwind is easy to use if you already master styling. But for those with little CSS experience, it creates a false sense of learning. It conveys that it is a minimalist way of writing CSS, taking away the effort of keeping your code tidy. Using so many pre-built classes hinders a developer's ability to truly master CSS. The time you save naming classes you lose learning to use the framework in the most efficient way.

sentences.en: Tailwind is easy to use if you already master styling.
sentences.zh: 如果您已经掌握了造型，Tailwind 会很容易使用。

sentences.en: But for those with little CSS experience, it creates a false sense of learning.
sentences.zh: 但对于那些 CSS 经验很少的人来说，这会产生一种错误的学习感觉。

sentences.en: It conveys that it is a minimalist way of writing CSS, taking away the effort of keeping your code tidy.
sentences.zh: 它表明这是一种极简的 CSS 编写方式，无需费力保持代码整洁。

sentences.en: Using so many pre-built classes hinders a developer's ability to truly master CSS.
sentences.zh: 使用如此多的预构建类会阻碍开发人员真正掌握 CSS 的能力。

sentences.en: The time you save naming classes you lose learning to use the framework in the most efficient way.
sentences.zh: 当你节省命名类的时间时，你就失去了以最有效的方式使用框架的知识。

blocks.html_en: On the other hand, if you go deep into Tailwind, you drift away from learning the fundamentals of the platform. pt-4 forces you to mentally translate to padding-top: 1rem. You gain fluency in the abstraction, not in CSS. To my students and coworkers I recommend learning CSS before Tailwind. And if you are already an experienced developer, you might not even need the framework.

sentences.en: On the other hand, if you go deep into Tailwind, you drift away from learning the fundamentals of the platform.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，如果您深入研究 Tailwind，您就会偏离学习该平台的基础知识。

sentences.en: pt-4 forces you to mentally translate to padding-top: 1rem.
sentences.zh: pt-4 迫使你在心里翻译成 padding-top: 1rem。

sentences.en: You gain fluency in the abstraction, not in CSS.
sentences.zh: 你会在抽象中获得流畅，而不是在 CSS 中。

sentences.en: To my students and coworkers I recommend learning CSS before Tailwind.
sentences.zh: 对于我的学生和同事，我建议先学习 CSS，然后再学习 Tailwind。

sentences.en: And if you are already an experienced developer, you might not even need the framework.
sentences.zh: 如果您已经是经验丰富的开发人员，您甚至可能不需要该框架。

blocks.html_en: It is hard to read

sentences.en: It is hard to read
sentences.zh: 很难读

blocks.html_en: Let me show you a button with an indigo background, white text, semibold font, rounded corners, hover, and focus.

sentences.en: Let me show you a button with an indigo background, white text, semibold font, rounded corners, hover, and focus.
sentences.zh: 让我向您展示一个具有靛蓝色背景、白色文本、半粗体字体、圆角、悬停和焦点的按钮。

blocks.html_en: First in vanilla CSS. I will take the liberty of using variables for colors and spacing, and nesting for hover and focus, something compatible today with every browser.

sentences.en: First in vanilla CSS.
sentences.zh: 首先是原生 CSS。

sentences.en: I will take the liberty of using variables for colors and spacing, and nesting for hover and focus, something compatible today with every browser.
sentences.zh: 我将冒昧地使用颜色和间距变量，以及悬停和焦点嵌套，这些现在与每个浏览器兼容。

blocks.html_en: Now in Tailwind CSS using @apply.

sentences.en: Now in Tailwind CSS using @apply.
sentences.zh: 现在在 Tailwind CSS 中使用 @apply。

blocks.html_en: Vanilla CSS is self-explanatory, whereas with Tailwind you have to check the documentation. What color is bg-indigo-500? How round is rounded-lg? Is bg-indigo-700 darker than bg-indigo-500? The first snippet is easier to maintain, the learning curve for a new developer is low, and the CSS tends to be modular. You do put in more effort with vanilla CSS, yes, but only at the start. Afterward you have full control of variables, cascade, and naming.

sentences.en: Vanilla CSS is self-explanatory, whereas with Tailwind you have to check the documentation.
sentences.zh: Vanilla CSS 是不言自明的，而使用 Tailwind 你必须检查文档。

sentences.en: What color is bg-indigo-500?
sentences.zh: bg-indigo-500 是什么颜色？

sentences.en: How round is rounded-lg?
sentences.zh: rounded-lg 有多圆？

sentences.en: Is bg-indigo-700 darker than bg-indigo-500?
sentences.zh: bg-indigo-700 比 bg-indigo-500 更黑吗？

sentences.en: The first snippet is easier to maintain, the learning curve for a new developer is low, and the CSS tends to be modular.
sentences.zh: 第一个片段更容易维护，新开发人员的学习曲线较低，并且 CSS 趋于模块化。

sentences.en: You do put in more effort with vanilla CSS, yes, but only at the start.
sentences.zh: 是的，你确实在普通 CSS 上投入了更多的精力，但只是在一开始。

sentences.en: Afterward you have full control of variables, cascade, and naming.
sentences.zh: 之后您就可以完全控制变量、级联和命名。

blocks.html_en: A curious detail. The example above uses @apply, and Adam Wathan himself has admitted that @apply "basically only exists to trick people" and that if he started Tailwind from scratch he would not include it. In other words, the route you use to recover the readability of a normal class contradicts Tailwind's philosophy. And if you do not use @apply, then you swallow the class soup in your HTML.

sentences.en: A curious detail.
sentences.zh: 一个令人好奇的细节。

sentences.en: The example above uses @apply, and Adam Wathan himself has admitted that @apply "basically only exists to trick people" and that if he started Tailwind from scratch he would not include it.
sentences.zh: 上面的例子使用了 @apply，Adam Wathan 本人也承认 @apply“基本上只是为了欺骗人们而存在”，如果他从头开始启动 Tailwind，他就不会包含它。

sentences.en: In other words, the route you use to recover the readability of a normal class contradicts Tailwind's philosophy.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，您用来恢复正常类的可读性的路线与 Tailwind 的理念相矛盾。

sentences.en: And if you do not use @apply, then you swallow the class soup in your HTML.
sentences.zh: 如果你不使用@apply，那么你就吞下了 HTML 中的类汤。

blocks.html_en: The HTML lies to you about priority

sentences.en: The HTML lies to you about priority
sentences.zh: HTML 在优先级方面向您撒谎

blocks.html_en: You may have heard that Tailwind "ignores the cascade". That is an imprecise way to put it, because the real problem is more subtle and interesting.

sentences.en: You may have heard that Tailwind "ignores the cascade".
sentences.zh: 您可能听说过 Tailwind“忽略级联”。

sentences.en: That is an imprecise way to put it, because the real problem is more subtle and interesting.
sentences.zh: 这是一种不精确的说法，因为真正的问题更加微妙和有趣。

blocks.html_en: Being able to control which selector wins based on its position in the stylesheet is fundamental to any architecture. A typical mistake among inexperienced web designers is to believe that the order of the classes in the HTML determines which one wins. It does not. Look at this code.

sentences.en: Being able to control which selector wins based on its position in the stylesheet is fundamental to any architecture.
sentences.zh: 能够根据样式表中的位置来控制哪个选择器获胜是任何架构的基础。

sentences.en: A typical mistake among inexperienced web designers is to believe that the order of the classes in the HTML determines which one wins.
sentences.zh: 缺乏经验的 Web 设计者的一个典型错误是相信 HTML 中类的顺序决定了哪一个获胜。

sentences.en: It does not.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Look at this code.
sentences.zh: 看看这段代码。

blocks.html_en: What color is it? You do not know. You need to see the CSS cascade.

sentences.en: What color is it?
sentences.zh: 它是什么颜色？

sentences.en: You do not know.
sentences.zh: 你不知道。

sentences.en: You need to see the CSS cascade.
sentences.zh: 您需要查看 CSS 级联。

blocks.html_en: Now yes, it is red, because .color-red is defined later. So far, normal CSS.

sentences.en: Now yes, it is red, because .color-red is defined later.
sentences.zh: 现在是的，它是红色的，因为 .color-red 是稍后定义的。

sentences.en: So far, normal CSS.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，正常的CSS。

blocks.html_en: The problem with Tailwind is that you cannot resolve this ambiguity even by reordering your classes. Watch.

sentences.en: The problem with Tailwind is that you cannot resolve this ambiguity even by reordering your classes.
sentences.zh: Tailwind 的问题在于，即使通过重新排序类也无法解决这种歧义。

sentences.en: Watch.
sentences.zh: 手表。

blocks.html_en: You might think green wins, since it comes last in the attribute. Well, no, you get red. What wins is decided by the order in which Tailwind generates those classes in the final stylesheet, not the order in which you write them in the HTML. The markup lies to you. Reading the HTML you cannot know the result. And you do not fix it by changing the order of the classes, because that order is controlled by the compiler. You are left with !important or with avoiding conflicting utilities. This is what is called a leaky abstraction. It promises you simplicity and forces you to know how it works underneath. Another classic case, class="mt-4 mt-0" does not do what its order suggests.

sentences.en: You might think green wins, since it comes last in the attribute.
sentences.zh: 您可能认为绿色获胜，因为它在属性中排在最后。

sentences.en: Well, no, you get red.
sentences.zh: 好吧，不，你会脸红。

sentences.en: What wins is decided by the order in which Tailwind generates those classes in the final stylesheet, not the order in which you write them in the HTML.
sentences.zh: 胜出取决于 Tailwind 在最终样式表中生成这些类的顺序，而不是您在 HTML 中编写它们的顺序。

sentences.en: The markup lies to you.
sentences.zh: 标记对你撒谎。

sentences.en: Reading the HTML you cannot know the result.
sentences.zh: 阅读 HTML 您无法知道结果。

sentences.en: And you do not fix it by changing the order of the classes, because that order is controlled by the compiler.
sentences.zh: 并且您不能通过更改类的顺序来修复它，因为该顺序是由编译器控制的。

sentences.en: You are left with !important or with avoiding conflicting utilities.
sentences.zh: 您只剩下 !important 或避免冲突的实用程序。

sentences.en: This is what is called a leaky abstraction.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的泄漏抽象。

sentences.en: It promises you simplicity and forces you to know how it works underneath.
sentences.zh: 它向您承诺简单性并迫使您了解它的底层工作原理。

sentences.en: Another classic case, class="mt-4 mt-0" does not do what its order suggests.
sentences.zh: 另一个经典案例，class="mt-4 mt-0" 并不按照其顺序执行。

blocks.html_en: Working with Dev Tools is not comfortable

sentences.en: Working with Dev Tools is not comfortable
sentences.zh: 使用开发工具并不舒服

blocks.html_en: When you build components with tons of classes, checking in the inspector which styles apply becomes slow. You have to scroll looking for what wins and what gets overridden. With vanilla CSS you quickly see which styles are there and in what order, and an error is easier to locate. It is true that editor extensions ease this at writing time, but in the browser, debugging in production, the class soup is still there.

sentences.en: When you build components with tons of classes, checking in the inspector which styles apply becomes slow.
sentences.zh: 当您构建具有大量类的组件时，在检查器中检查应用哪些样式会变得很慢。

sentences.en: You have to scroll looking for what wins and what gets overridden.
sentences.zh: 您必须滚动查找哪些内容获胜以及哪些内容被覆盖。

sentences.en: With vanilla CSS you quickly see which styles are there and in what order, and an error is easier to locate.
sentences.zh: 使用 vanilla CSS，您可以快速查看其中有哪些样式以及顺序，并且更容易找到错误。

sentences.en: It is true that editor extensions ease this at writing time, but in the browser, debugging in production, the class soup is still there.
sentences.zh: 确实，编辑器扩展在编写时缓解了这个问题，但在浏览器中，在生产中调试时，类汤仍然存在。

blocks.html_en: Conclusion

sentences.en: Conclusion
sentences.zh: 结论

blocks.html_en: What if you just use modern CSS?

sentences.en: What if you just use modern CSS?
sentences.zh: 如果你只使用现代 CSS 会怎样？

blocks.html_en: Here is, for me, the truly fresh debate. It is no longer "utilities versus CSS by hand". It is "native modern CSS versus a utility layer on top".

sentences.en: Here is, for me, the truly fresh debate.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这是真正新鲜的辩论。

sentences.en: It is no longer "utilities versus CSS by hand".
sentences.zh: 它不再是“实用程序与手动 CSS”的问题。

sentences.en: It is "native modern CSS versus a utility layer on top".
sentences.zh: 它是“原生现代 CSS 与顶部的实用层”。

blocks.html_en: Look at what the platform gives you today, without installing anything:

sentences.en: Look at what the platform gives you today, without installing anything:
sentences.zh: 看看该平台今天为您提供了什么，无需安装任何东西：

blocks.html_en: • Cascade layers (@layer) to order priority without fighting specificity.

sentences.en: Cascade layers (@layer) to order priority without fighting specificity.
sentences.zh: 级联层（@layer）来排序优先级，而不需要对抗特殊性。

blocks.html_en: • Native nesting, now without a preprocessor.

sentences.en: Native nesting, now without a preprocessor.
sentences.zh: 原生嵌套，现在没有预处理器。

blocks.html_en: • Custom properties (CSS variables) for your tokens.

sentences.en: Custom properties (CSS variables) for your tokens.
sentences.zh: 令牌的自定义属性（CSS 变量）。

blocks.html_en: • :has(), the parent selector we had been asking for over twenty years.

sentences.en: :has(), the parent selector we had been asking for over twenty years.
sentences.zh: :has()，我们二十多年来一直要求的父选择器。

blocks.html_en: • Container queries for per-component responsiveness.

sentences.en: Container queries for per-component responsiveness.
sentences.zh: 容器查询每个组件的响应能力。

blocks.html_en: • color-mix() to derive colors.

sentences.en: color-mix() to derive colors.
sentences.zh: color-mix() 派生颜色。

blocks.html_en: And you know what the ironic part is? That Tailwind is built right on top of those same features. It uses native cascade layers, @property, container queries, and OKLCH colors. Which gives ammunition to the most uncomfortable argument. If the platform already brings all that, how much of Tailwind is still essential?

sentences.en: And you know what the ironic part is?
sentences.zh: 你知道讽刺的部分是什么吗？

sentences.en: That Tailwind is built right on top of those same features.
sentences.zh: Tailwind 正是建立在这些相同功能之上的。

sentences.en: It uses native cascade layers, @property, container queries, and OKLCH colors.
sentences.zh: 它使用本机级联层、@property、容器查询和 OKLCH 颜色。

sentences.en: Which gives ammunition to the most uncomfortable argument.
sentences.zh: 这为最令人不安的争论提供了弹药。

sentences.en: If the platform already brings all that, how much of Tailwind is still essential?
sentences.zh: 如果平台已经实现了这一切，那么 Tailwind 有多少仍然是必不可少的？

blocks.html_en: The counterpart is clear. Native CSS gives you the features, but it does not give you the system of constraints, nor the style kept next to the markup (colocation), nor autocomplete. On small or server-rendered projects, modern CSS on its own is a great option. On a large product built with components and with many people touching it, Tailwind still has arguments. There is no universal winner, there is a context.

sentences.en: The counterpart is clear.
sentences.zh: 对方很清楚。

sentences.en: Native CSS gives you the features, but it does not give you the system of constraints, nor the style kept next to the markup (colocation), nor autocomplete.
sentences.zh: 原生 CSS 为您提供了功能，但它没有为您提供约束系统，也没有提供标记旁边的样式（并置），也没有提供自动完成功能。

sentences.en: On small or server-rendered projects, modern CSS on its own is a great option.
sentences.zh: 在小型或服务器渲染项目中，现代 CSS 本身就是一个不错的选择。

sentences.en: On a large product built with components and with many people touching it, Tailwind still has arguments.
sentences.zh: 对于一个由组件构建且有很多人接触的大型产品，Tailwind 仍然存在争议。

sentences.en: There is no universal winner, there is a context.
sentences.zh: 没有普遍的赢家，只有一个背景。

blocks.html_en: But let us put things in perspective. It is not a bad tool. It is a tool with a cost you pay in the future, and one that nowadays also competes with a native CSS far more capable than a few years ago. Before choosing it, learn CSS. Then decide with knowledge. The initial effort you save today, you may pay back with interest tomorrow. Or maybe not. Now, at least, you have both sides to decide for yourself.

sentences.en: But let us put things in perspective.
sentences.zh: 但让我们正确看待事情。

sentences.en: It is not a bad tool.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个坏工具。

sentences.en: It is a tool with a cost you pay in the future, and one that nowadays also competes with a native CSS far more capable than a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 它是一种需要你在未来付出代价的工具，而且现在它还可以与比几年前功能强大得多的原生 CSS 竞争。

sentences.en: Before choosing it, learn CSS.
sentences.zh: 在选择它之前，先学习CSS。

sentences.en: Then decide with knowledge.
sentences.zh: 然后用知识来决定。

sentences.en: The initial effort you save today, you may pay back with interest tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 今天你存下的最初的努力，明天你可能会连本带利地偿还。

sentences.en: Or maybe not.
sentences.zh: 或者也许不是。

sentences.en: Now, at least, you have both sides to decide for yourself.
sentences.zh: 现在，至少，双方都可以自己决定。

sentences.zh: Tailwind CSS、Script Raccoon 的缺点。

content_html_zh:
Tailwind CSS 是 Web 开发人员中非常流行的 CSS 框架。 无需任何图形设计知识，它就能为您解决间距、颜色和尺寸的标准化问题。 最重要的是，如果你稍微有点混乱，它就会迫使你采用一种基于从简单的实用程序构建大型结构的工作方法（实用程序优先基础知识）。 除此之外，还可以通过完美的搜索添加易于理解的文档。

过去我在几个项目中使用过它，它帮助我快速构建用户界面。 尽管如此，我并不在所有情况下都推荐使用它。 我将向您阐述我的观点、我的理由以及为什么您在中型或大型项目中使用 Tailwind CSS 之前应该三思而后行。 我对你们唯一的要求就是开放的心态、自我批评和学习的意愿。

你要学几十门课

Tailwind 有数千个实用程序类。 尽管文档非常好并且编辑器自动完成功能也有很大帮助，但您必须内化的基本类还是有上限的。 最有可能的是，一开始您将在浏览器选项卡打开且搜索框不间断工作的情况下进行开发。 您花时间了解应用每门课程的最合适方法。 一开始是一个缓慢的过程。 如果您创建了自己的类并与 Tailwind 的类混合，那么难度就会增加。

它打破了结构和设计之间的分离

Tailwind CSS 是一个巨大的实用程序库，具有特定工作的原子类。 除非您使用 @apply 对类进行分组，否则您最终会在 HTML 中包含数十个类。 这打破了结构与设计分离、HTML 与 CSS 分离的经典规则。 它使 HTML 变得臃肿，可读性受到影响，并且失去了可重用性。

也就是说，这一点值得暂停，因为这是最受反驳的批评。 Tailwind 的创建者 Adam Wathan 撰写了辩护的基础文本，他的论点很好。 关注点分离并没有消失，而是改变了方向。 使用“语义”CSS，您的 CSS 依赖于 HTML；您可以重新设计 HTML，但您的 CSS 不可重用。 使用实用程序，您的 HTML 取决于 CSS； CSS 是可重用的，但 HTML 不会自行重新设计样式。 两种情况都存在耦合，只是箭头的方向发生了变化。

这个论点在组件世界中成立，React 或 Vue 已经将逻辑、标记和样式放在同一个文件中。 在那里，按文件类型的分隔已经被您事先打破了。 但在使用模板和经典 CSS 的服务器渲染项目中，这种分离仍然完全有意义。 这不是普遍法则，而是取决于您的架构的决定。

其名称并不一致

它的命名并不总是连贯的，有时是不透明的并且容易造成混乱。 查看对齐类。 items-center、justify-center、text-center 和 place-content-center 之间有什么区别？ 该名称不直观且不遵循清晰的模式。 如果您好奇，items-center 可以在 Flex 容器中对齐项目，justify-center 可以在主轴上对齐它们，text-center 可以使文本居中，而 place-content-center 可以使网格中的内容居中。 让我重命名它们以寻求连贯性：flex-align-items-center、flex-justify-content-center、text-align-center 和 grid-place-items-center。 你注意到其中的区别了吗？

还有更多的例子： justify-center 但 items-center （不是align-center）； border 给出 1px，但 border-2 给出 2px。 小摩擦累积起来。

设计系统并没有像看起来那样得到执行

支持 Tailwind 的一大论据是它的间距和色阶迫使你保持一致。 这是事实，但有一个问题，即任意值。 您可以编写 w-[347px]、text-[#1a2b3c] 或 p-[5.5rem]，而无需任何警告。 它们是破坏系统的逃生口。 没有什么可以阻止您在同一项目中使用 sky-400 和 blue-400。 一致性仍然取决于你的纪律，而不是框架。 系统可以帮助你，但它不能拯救你自己。

这不是学习 CSS 的好门户

如果您已经掌握了造型，Tailwind 会很容易使用。 但对于那些 CSS 经验很少的人来说，这会产生一种错误的学习感觉。 它表明这是一种极简的 CSS 编写方式，无需费力保持代码整洁。 使用如此多的预构建类会阻碍开发人员真正掌握 CSS 的能力。 当你节省命名类的时间时，你就失去了以最有效的方式使用框架的知识。

另一方面，如果您深入研究 Tailwind，您就会偏离学习该平台的基础知识。 pt-4 迫使你在心里翻译成 padding-top: 1rem。 你会在抽象中获得流畅，而不是在 CSS 中。 对于我的学生和同事，我建议先学习 CSS，然后再学习 Tailwind。 如果您已经是经验丰富的开发人员，您甚至可能不需要该框架。

很难读

让我向您展示一个具有靛蓝色背景、白色文本、半粗体字体、圆角、悬停和焦点的按钮。

首先是原生 CSS。 我将冒昧地使用颜色和间距变量，以及悬停和焦点嵌套，这些现在与每个浏览器兼容。

:root {
  --color-white: #fff;
  --color-black: #000;
  --color-indigo: #4f46e5;
  --color-indigo-hover: #4338ca;
  --gap-s: 0.5rem;
  --gap-m: 1rem;
}

.button {
    padding: var(--gap-s) var(--gap-m);
    background-color: var(--color-indigo);
    color: var(--color-white);
    font-weight: 700;
    border-radius: var(--gap-s);
    &:hover, &:focus {
        background-color: var(--color-indigo-hover);
    }
}

现在在 Tailwind CSS 中使用 @apply。

.button {
    @apply py-2 px-4 bg-indigo-500 text-white font-semibold rounded-lg hover:bg-indigo-700 focus:bg-indigo-700;
}

Vanilla CSS 是不言自明的，而使用 Tailwind 你必须检查文档。 bg-indigo-500 是什么颜色？ rounded-lg 有多圆？ bg-indigo-700 比 bg-indigo-500 更黑吗？ 第一个片段更容易维护，新开发人员的学习曲线较低，并且 CSS 趋于模块化。 是的，你确实在普通 CSS 上投入了更多的精力，但只是在一开始。 之后您就可以完全控制变量、级联和命名。

一个令人好奇的细节。 上面的例子使用了 @apply，Adam Wathan 本人也承认 @apply“基本上只是为了欺骗人们而存在”，如果他从头开始启动 Tailwind，他就不会包含它。 换句话说，您用来恢复正常类的可读性的路线与 Tailwind 的理念相矛盾。 如果你不使用@apply，那么你就吞下了 HTML 中的类汤。

HTML 在优先级方面向您撒谎

您可能听说过 Tailwind“忽略级联”。 这是一种不精确的说法，因为真正的问题更加微妙和有趣。

能够根据样式表中的位置来控制哪个选择器获胜是任何架构的基础。 缺乏经验的 Web 设计者的一个典型错误是相信 HTML 中类的顺序决定了哪一个获胜。 事实并非如此。 看看这段代码。

<p class="color-red color-green">I am some text</p>

它是什么颜色？ 你不知道。 您需要查看 CSS 级联。

.color-green {
    color: green;
}

.color-red {
    color: red;
}

现在是的，它是红色的，因为 .color-red 是稍后定义的。 到目前为止，正常的CSS。

Tailwind 的问题在于，即使通过重新排序类也无法解决这种歧义。 手表。

<p class="text-red-500 text-green-500">I am some text</p>

您可能认为绿色获胜，因为它在属性中排在最后。 好吧，不，你会脸红。 胜出取决于 Tailwind 在最终样式表中生成这些类的顺序，而不是您在 HTML 中编写它们的顺序。 标记对你撒谎。 阅读 HTML 您无法知道结果。 并且您不能通过更改类的顺序来修复它，因为该顺序是由编译器控制的。 您只剩下 !important 或避免冲突的实用程序。 这就是所谓的泄漏抽象。 它向您承诺简单性并迫使您了解它的底层工作原理。 另一个经典案例，class="mt-4 mt-0" 并不按照其顺序执行。

使用开发工具并不舒服

当您构建具有大量类的组件时，在检查器中检查应用哪些样式会变得很慢。 您必须滚动查找哪些内容获胜以及哪些内容被覆盖。 使用 vanilla CSS，您可以快速查看其中有哪些样式以及顺序，并且更容易找到错误。 确实，编辑器扩展在编写时缓解了这个问题，但在浏览器中，在生产中调试时，类汤仍然存在。

结论

如果你只使用现代 CSS 会怎样？

对我来说，这是真正新鲜的辩论。 它不再是“实用程序与手动 CSS”的问题。 它是“原生现代 CSS 与顶部的实用层”。

看看该平台今天为您提供了什么，无需安装任何东西：

  • 级联层（@layer）来排序优先级，而不需要对抗特殊性。
  • 原生嵌套，现在没有预处理器。
  • 令牌的自定义属性（CSS 变量）。
  • :has()，我们二十多年来一直要求的父选择器。
  • 容器查询每个组件的响应能力。
  • color-mix() 派生颜色。

你知道讽刺的部分是什么吗？ Tailwind 正是建立在这些相同功能之上的。 它使用本机级联层、@property、容器查询和 OKLCH 颜色。 这为最令人不安的争论提供了弹药。 如果平台已经实现了这一切，那么 Tailwind 有多少仍然是必不可少的？

对方很清楚。 原生 CSS 为您提供了功能，但它没有为您提供约束系统，也没有提供标记旁边的样式（并置），也没有提供自动完成功能。 在小型或服务器渲染项目中，现代 CSS 本身就是一个不错的选择。 对于一个由组件构建且有很多人接触的大型产品，Tailwind 仍然存在争议。 没有普遍的赢家，只有一个背景。

但让我们正确看待事情。 这不是一个坏工具。 它是一种需要你在未来付出代价的工具，而且现在它还可以与比几年前功能强大得多的原生 CSS 竞争。 在选择它之前，先学习CSS。 然后用知识来决定。 今天你存下的最初的努力，明天你可能会连本带利地偿还。 或者也许不是。 现在，至少，双方都可以自己决定。

来源

  • 开源我们在 Tailwind CSS v4.0 上的进展，官方 Tailwind 博客（新引擎、带有 @theme 的 CSS-first 配置以及性能数据）。
  • 为什么我不喜欢 Tailwind CSS，Aleksandr Hovhannisyan。
